name: Montana
dueDateNotes: Montana follows the federal schedule: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15. If a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.
selfEmploymentNotes: Montana starts from your federal taxable income (so the federal standard deduction is already baked in; there is no separate Montana deduction to subtract) and applies a two-rate schedule: 4.7% up to $47,500 (single) or $95,000 (married), and 5.65% above. The top rate is scheduled to fall to 5.4% in 2027. Long-term capital gains are taxed at separate, lower rates (3.0% / 4.1%), not the ordinary rates shown here.
uniqueFacts: Montana taxes long-term capital gains at separate, lower rates (3.0% and 4.1%) instead of the ordinary income rates.
Montana's top income tax rate is scheduled to drop from 5.65% to 5.4% in 2027.
Montana begins from your federal taxable income, so it has no separate state standard deduction to claim on top of the federal one.
